transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-31
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (Verdance Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Verdance Infra Lead), Elena Ortiz (Verdance Solutions Arch)

Summary: Exploratory intro between Verdance Systems (SI) and Redwood to scope GPU orchestration and onramp integration. High-level goals: understand Verdance's multi-tenant deployment patterns, confirm network/KMS and VPC constraints, and identify initial pilot metrics (latency, cost, throughput).

Topics: partner onboarding, dedicated vs hosted routing, VPC/private deployments, SOC2/KMS/SSO requirements, sample benchmarks, pilot timeline

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off — I'm Avery, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya here, Head of AI at Verdance. We're an SI that embeds LLMs into customer SaaS. Marcus and Elena are on infra and solutions.
[00:21] Marcus: Marcus, infra. We run a mix of cloud and some colo sites for latency sensitive clients.
[00:27] Elena: Elena, solutions architect, I look after deployment patterns and integration.
[00:32] Diego: Diego, SE from Redwood, I handle performance + private deployments.
[00:36] Samir: Samir, CSM, happy to help coordinate pilots and business ops.
[00:40] Avery: Great. High level: Verdance wants a partner to offload inference orchestration and offer an onramp for your customers. Today you mostly stitch open-source runtimes and custom autoscaling?
[00:52] Priya: Yeah that's right. We have a lot of bespoke scripts, some Kubernetes operators, and we end up rewriting scheduling logic per customer. Time to market is a problem.
[01:05] Diego: Makes sense. Can you walk through the traffic profile—are you doing bursty per-tenant, mostly chat-like sessions, or long context batches?
[01:15] Elena: Mixed. A few customers send long context (6k-8k) occasionally for analytics, but most are conversational bursts with lots of short calls. We need predictable p99 latency under 600ms for certain SLAs.
[01:28] Marcus: Also budget pressure: some customers want hosted pay-per-call, others need dedicated pools and cost predictability.
[01:37] Avery: That aligns with how customers use Redwood: we support hosted API, Dedicated reservations, and Private VPC deployments. Quick clarification on data flow—do your customers require on-prem inference or is VPC enough?
[01:48] Priya: For finance and healthcare customers, on-prem or air-gapped is sometimes required. VPC with strong KMS integration could be okay for mid-market.
[01:58] Diego: Noted. We have a Private product that supports customer-managed control plane and can integrate with KMS/HSM for key wrapping. We should get into the specifics later — things like supported KMS providers and whether you need HSM attestation.
[02:12] Priya: Yes, HSM would be preferred for a handful of clients. Also audit logs - long retention for compliance.
[02:20] Samir: Redwood supports audit logs and can configure retention; we also integrate with S3/ELK for exports.
[02:26] Marcus: On networking, we currently use VPC peering for some customers and direct connect for others. Can Redwood handle direct peering and private links?
[02:35] Diego: Yes, we support VPC peering and private link-esque setups. For on-prem we typically have an agent for networking handshake. We should capture your exact topology.
[02:45] Elena: Perfect. On the orchestration side, how does Redwood deal with model variants and fallbacks? We often need a smaller quantized model during peak to preserve latency.
[02:56] Diego: We do smart routing: policy-based routing can send requests to a cheaper quantized variant if p95 latency exceeds targets or if Dedicated capacity is saturated. Also continuous batching and prefix/KV cache helps reduce cost for repeated prompts. The KV cache we call K-V cache in docs, sometimes spelled K V cache in old notes — sorry the transcriber messes with that.
[03:16] Priya: That's great. We need to see how your quantization impacts quality; our customers are sensitive to hallucinations.
[03:23] Diego: Totally. We provide eval harnesses tied to prompt sets so you can monitor quality regressions. We can also do canary rollouts and A/B tests per customer.
[03:33] Avery: Curious — what are your target success criteria for a pilot? Latency, cost, integration effort?
[03:40] Priya: Pilot success is twofold: 1) meet p95 latency SLA for chat customers (<400ms for basic customers, <600ms for premium), and 2) demonstrate 20-30% cost improvement on token spend for long-running batch workloads via batching + cache.
[03:56] Marcus: Also we want an integration that replicates our tenancy model so we don't have to rewrite auth and routing for each customer.
[04:03] Diego: We can support multi-tenant mapping and route tokens by tenant ID. We expose per-route metrics and token-level cost breakdowns in the Console.
[04:12] Elena: How intrusive is the integration? We prefer agents + light control plane integration rather than full lift-and-shift.
[04:20] Diego: For Private deployments we typically install a small control-plane agent and a local connector for telemetry and cache. Most heavy-lifting stays in your cluster or our dedicated pools depending on mode.
[04:31] Priya: Any constraints on GPU vendors? We run mixed NVIDIA A100s and some Ampere alternatives at colo.
[04:39] Diego: We support NVIDIA stacks out-of-the-box; for alternative accelerators we need to validate kernels and compilation paths. We do kernel selection per-model and per-hardware. If you want, we can run a compatibility sweep across your hardware during the pilot.
[04:53] Avery: Quick question about compliance — SSO and provisioning: we use SAML/SSO, RBAC and we have enterprise SSO docs.
[05:02] Priya: We use Okta and SAML, and require SCIM for provisioning. Also require SOC2 + ISO27001 for vendor paperwork.
[05:11] Samir: We have SOC2 reports and can share a SOC2 letter; we also support SAML/SCIM integrations. I'll include the security pack in the follow-up.
[05:18] Marcus: What about key management? We need customer-controlled keys with rotation.
[05:24] Diego: We support customer-managed keys with KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM options in Private. Rotation and key wrapping supported.
[05:31] Elena: Great. Pricing structure question: Verdance wants to resell — how do partner margins or committed capacity deals work?
[05:39] Avery: We have partner pricing for Dedicated and reseller contracts; we'll share the partner playbook. For pilots we usually do a short-term committed bucket to hit repeatable bandwidth for evaluation.
[05:48] Priya: For the first customer pilot we might need a dedicated small pool to guarantee latency.
[05:53] Diego: We can carve a small Dedicated pool for the pilot and route only that tenant to it. If traffic spikes you can fall back to hosted or quantized model variants.
[06:03] Priya: About benchmarks — can you run an example with our typical payloads? We have prompt templates and chat history that are fairly specific.
[06:11] Diego: Yes, please share a set of sanitized prompt examples. We'll run two scenarios: low-latency chat (2-3 tokens per turn, short context) and long-context analytic runs (6k–8k) and return traces.
[06:22] Elena: We'll share both. Also, we need to measure memory usage and tokenization overhead.
[06:27] Diego: We'll include tokenization breakdowns and per-request memory footprints in the trace.
[06:32] Priya: On handoffs — who's the single point from Redwood for the technical work?
[06:36] Avery: Diego is primary for tech, Samir will coordinate the pilot ops and legal. I'm the commercial lead.
[06:42] Marcus: Perfect. A couple of technical nitty-gritty: do you support direct NVLINK access or GPU-passthrough for custom kernels?
[06:50] Diego: For private on-prem we can support GPU passthrough if needed, but that increases operational complexity. We'll need your kernel builds and to run new compilation. Most customers prefer optimized kernels without full passthrough.
[07:03] Priya: Understood. Also, can we limit model weights from leaving the colo? Some customers don't want weights outside their premises.
[07:11] Diego: That's a common ask. Private deployments can be air-gapped with local weights; we can provide an on-prem package. We'll note an NDA process if we need to ship model artifacts.
[07:23] Elena: On latency targets — we mentioned p95 400–600ms. For long context batch jobs, do you have batching policies that preserve throughput without blowing up latency?
[07:34] Diego: We use workload-aware batching. For analytics jobs we favor throughput and may accept higher latency, but you can set per-route SLOs and specify max batching windows. The runtime will respect frequent flush thresholds for low-latency routes.
[07:50] Priya: Do you have any tooling for cost modeling? We need to show customers expected token spend across models and quantization levels.
[07:58] Avery: Redwood Optimize includes cost/performance tooling and model recommendation engine. Diego can demo a sample cost model for your prompt set.
[08:06] Diego: I'll prepare a spreadsheet with token-level cost, expected latency, and recommended quantization for each workload.
[08:11] Priya: On security again — can you provide proof of secure erase and data retention policies? Some clients require deletion certifications.
[08:19] Samir: We can provide retention docs and support deletion workflows; we'll surface our data retention matrix and logs export options.
[08:26] Marcus: For pilot instrumentation we need to ingest traces into our monitoring stack. Do you export traces to OTLP or Jaeger?
[08:33] Diego: Yes, we support OTLP and Jaeger and can stream metrics and logs into your telemetry pipeline.
[08:40] Elena: Any caveats with multi-region routing and fallbacks? We have users in EMEA and APAC.
[08:48] Diego: We have smart routing by region and capacity tiers; if a region is constrained, requests can fallback to another region with policy-defined fallbacks. We can prioritize data residency if required.
[08:59] Priya: That will be crucial for a European finance client.
[09:03] Avery: Sounds like we have a lot to tack. Quick logistics: we'll share a partner onboarding deck, an integration checklist, and a benchmark template. We propose a pilot timeline: week 0–1: onboarding & infra review; week 2: run benchmarks; week 3: analyze and tune; week 4: demo results and decision. Does that timeline fit?
[09:22] Priya: That seems reasonable. We'll need legal/NDAs signed early, though.
[09:27] Samir: We'll push the security pack and the standard MSA template after this call.
[09:32] Marcus: On the benchmarks — will you include both hosted and dedicated run numbers so we can compare?
[09:37] Diego: Yes, we'll run hosted API baseline and Dedicated pool runs and include quantized variants.
[09:42] Elena: Any risk areas we should flag?
[09:45] Diego: Potential areas: compatibility with non-standard accelerators, need for kernel tuning, and any customers with ultra-strict weight residency. Also, integration time for SCIM/SSO provisioning can vary across enterprise customers.
[09:59] Priya: We're okay with that. Regarding resell — can Redwood support co-branded provisioning or white-labeling?
[10:06] Avery: We have partner programs that allow limited co-branding in the console and resell terms. We'll follow up with the partner playbook.
[10:14] Diego: I'll also include a simple runbook for tenant isolation and mapping.
[10:19] Priya: Sounds good. Any questions from Redwood?
[10:22] Avery: One last thing — do you have a preference for initial pilot customers? A low-risk internal customer or a production customer?
[10:31] Priya: We'll start internal-ish—an existing client on non-critical workflows to avoid safety issues.
[10:36] Samir: Perfect. We'll draft the pilot statement of work.
[10:40] Avery: Awesome. I'll recap next steps — share deck, Diego does benchmarks, Priya shares infra and prompts, legal exchange NDA.
[10:48] Diego: Also note, we sometimes see transcription errors in Fireflies; the product name might appear as Redood or Redbwood in the raw export. Ignore that.
[10:56] Priya: Ha, noted.

[11:00] --- End of recording (approx 54 min) ---

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Avery to share partner onboarding deck and partner playbook (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/partner-onboarding)
- Diego to run hosted + dedicated benchmarks with Verdance prompt set and return traces (template: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/template)
- Priya to share infra diagram, SSO provider (Okta) details, and sanitized prompt payloads
- Samir to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and partner MSA template

Artifacts mentioned: partner-onboarding deck (link above), benchmark spreadsheet, sample runbook for tenant mapping.

Notes on transcription: speaker labels may be imprecise; occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K-V cache -> K V cache).
